I added `--since DATE` to `scripts/export.py`. It takes a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` and rejects anything else with a clear argparse error.

I only ran it against staging with `--dry-run`. A project memory warns that staging's `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket, which is left over from the 2025 migration. A real run would overwrite the prod invoice reports.

```
$ python3 scripts/export.py --env staging --since 2026-09-01 --dry-run
exporting staging to ledgerline-exports-dev since=2026-09-01 (dry_run=True)
```

`EXPORT_BUCKET` wasn't set in this shell, so it used the dev default bucket and didn't show the real staging configuration. Passing `--since not-a-date` failed as expected (`invalid fromisoformat value`).

The script doesn't export anything yet. It only parses the arguments and prints them, so `--since` is accepted and shown in the output but nothing filters by it. Once the export logic exists, it will need to use `args.since`.

If you want a real (non-dry-run) staging export, that needs your explicit go-ahead and ideally fixing staging's `EXPORT_BUCKET` first. I haven't changed anything else.
